title: An effaceable delta-functor is universal (Grothendieck)
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and $F=(F^n,\delta_F)$ a $\delta$-functor from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]. Suppose that for every $n>0$ and every object $A$ of $\mathcal A$ there is a monomorphism $u:A\to B$ (depending on $A$ and $n$) such that $F^n(u):F^n(A)\to F^n(B)$ is zero. Then $F$ is a universal $\delta$-functor [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]: for every $\delta$-functor $G=(G^n,\delta_G)$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ and every natural transformation $t:F^0\to G^0$ there is a unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $(t^n)_{n\ge0}:F\to G$ with $t^0=t$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), with its proof (induction on n through the cokernel description F^{n+1}(A)=Coker(F^n(B)->F^n(C)); the verification that t^{n+1} is a natural transformation is 'omitted' in Stacks and must be written out at the split)

proof.text: **Step 1 (notation; effacing short exact sequences exist).** Fix a $\delta$-functor $G=(G^n,\delta_G)$ from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ and a natural transformation $t:F^0\to G^0$. For a short exact sequence $E:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] write $\delta^n_{F,E}:F^n(C)\to F^{n+1}(A)$ and $\delta^n_{G,E}:G^n(C)\to G^{n+1}(A)$ for the connecting morphisms of [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]; call $A$ its left object. For $n\ge0$ call $E$ *$(n+1)$-effacing* if $F^{n+1}(f)=0$. Claim: every object $A$ is the left object of an $(n+1)$-effacing short exact sequence. Indeed $n+1>0$, so the hypothesis gives a monomorphism $u:A\to B$ with $F^{n+1}(u)=0$ (Stacks says 'injective morphism', which in an abelian category is a monomorphism, Stacks Lemma 010C (1)). Let $\pi:B\to C$ be a cokernel of $u$ (cokernels exist in $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-abelian]); by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (c), $E_u:0\to A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{\pi}C\to0$ is short exact, and it is $(n+1)$-effacing. (Stacks: 'choose an embedding $u:A\to B$ such that $F^{n+1}(u)=0$. Let $C=B/u(A)$'.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof, first sentences of the second paragraph; Lemma 010C (lemma-characterize-injective)

proof.text: **Step 2 ($\delta_F$ of an effacing sequence is an epimorphism and a cokernel of $F^n(g)$).** Let $E:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be $(n+1)$-effacing. Axiom (1) of the $\delta$-functor $F$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] says that $F^n(B)\xrightarrow{F^n(g)}F^n(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^n_{F,E}}F^{n+1}(A)\xrightarrow{F^{n+1}(f)}F^{n+1}(B)$ is a complex exact at $F^n(C)$ and at $F^{n+1}(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Since $F^{n+1}(f)=0$, exactness at $F^{n+1}(A)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (b) give that $\delta^n_{F,E}$ is an epimorphism. Then exactness at $F^n(C)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a) (with $h=F^n(g)$, $e=\delta^n_{F,E}$) give that $\delta^n_{F,E}$ is a cokernel of $F^n(g)$. Hence: (i) $\delta^n_{F,E}$ can be cancelled on the right ($x\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=y\circ\delta^n_{F,E}\Rightarrow x=y$); (ii) every $\varphi:F^n(C)\to W$ with $\varphi\circ F^n(g)=0$ is $\psi\circ\delta^n_{F,E}$ for a unique $\psi:F^{n+1}(A)\to W$. (Stacks: '$F^{n+1}(A)=\mathrm{Coker}(F^n(B)\to F^n(C))$ by our choice of $u$'.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof, 'The long exact cohomology sequence ... gives that F^{n+1}(A) = Coker(F^n(B) -> F^n(C)) by our choice of u'

proof.text:
**Step 3 (the candidate $\tau_E$).** Assume $t^n:F^n\to G^n$ is a natural transformation, and let $E:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ be $(n+1)$-effacing. Put $\varphi=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C:F^n(C)\to G^{n+1}(A)$. By naturality of $t^n$ at $g$, $\varphi\circ F^n(g)=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C\circ F^n(g)=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ G^n(g)\circ t^n_B$, and $\delta^n_{G,E}\circ G^n(g)=0$ because the long sequence of axiom (1) for $G$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] is exact, hence a complex [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. So $\varphi\circ F^n(g)=0$ and by Step 2 (ii) there is a unique $\tau_E:F^{n+1}(A)\to G^{n+1}(A)$ with
$(\spadesuit)\quad\tau_E\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C$.
Moreover any $\psi:F^{n+1}(A)\to G^{n+1}(A)$ with $\psi\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C$ equals $\tau_E$ (Step 2 (i)). This is Stacks' definition of $t^{n+1}_A$ via the square with $\delta_{F,A\to B\to C}$ and $\delta_{G,A\to B\to C}$; Stacks writes the top arrow as the map $\mathrm{Coker}(F^n(B)\to F^n(C))\to\mathrm{Coker}(G^n(B)\to G^n(C))$ induced by $t^n$, and composing with $\delta_G$ (which kills the image of $G^n(B)$) is exactly $\varphi$.

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof, the commutative square defining t^{n+1}_A

proof.text: **Step 4 (comparison along a morphism of effacing sequences).** Let $t^n$ be natural, let $E:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ and $E':0\to A'\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ be $(n+1)$-effacing, and let $(a,b,c):E\to E'$ be a morphism of short exact sequences ($bf=f'a$, $cg=g'b$). Then $\tau_{E'}\circ F^{n+1}(a)=G^{n+1}(a)\circ\tau_E$. Proof: $\tau_{E'}\circ F^{n+1}(a)\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=\tau_{E'}\circ\delta^n_{F,E'}\circ F^n(c)$ (axiom (2) for $F$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]) $=\delta^n_{G,E'}\circ t^n_{C'}\circ F^n(c)$ ($(\spadesuit)$ for $E'$) $=\delta^n_{G,E'}\circ G^n(c)\circ t^n_C$ (naturality of $t^n$ at $c$) $=G^{n+1}(a)\circ\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C$ (axiom (2) for $G$) $=G^{n+1}(a)\circ\tau_E\circ\delta^n_{F,E}$ ($(\spadesuit)$ for $E$); cancel the epimorphism $\delta^n_{F,E}$ (Step 2 (i)). (Not in Stacks, which omits the verification; written out by the agent.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof: the verification omitted there ('We omit the verification that this defines a transformation of functors'; 'clearly uniquely determined'), written out by the agent

proof.text: **Step 5 (an effacing sequence mapping to two given ones).** Let $E:0\to A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ and $E':0\to A'\xrightarrow{u'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ be $(n+1)$-effacing and $a:A\to A'$ a morphism. Let $B\oplus B'$ be a biproduct with $i_1,i_2,p_1,p_2$, $p_1i_1=\mathrm{id}$, $p_2i_2=\mathrm{id}$, $p_1i_2=0$, $p_2i_1=0$, $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=\mathrm{id}$ (an abelian category has finite biproducts [def-sp-abelian], with these identities [def-weil-additive-category]), and $w=i_1u+i_2u'a:A\to B\oplus B'$; composition being bilinear, $p_1w=u$ and $p_2w=u'a$. (i) $w$ is a monomorphism: $wx=wy$ gives $ux=p_1wx=p_1wy=uy$, so $x=y$. (ii) $F^{n+1}(w)=0$: $F^{n+1}$ is additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], so $\mathrm{id}=F^{n+1}(i_1p_1+i_2p_2)=F^{n+1}(i_1)F^{n+1}(p_1)+F^{n+1}(i_2)F^{n+1}(p_2)$ and $F^{n+1}(w)=F^{n+1}(i_1)F^{n+1}(u)+F^{n+1}(i_2)F^{n+1}(u')F^{n+1}(a)=0+0$. (iii) With $\pi_w:B\oplus B'\to C_w$ a cokernel of $w$, $E_w:0\to A\xrightarrow{w}B\oplus B'\xrightarrow{\pi_w}C_w\to0$ is short exact [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (c) and $(n+1)$-effacing. (iv) $gp_1w=gu=0$ and $g'p_2w=g'u'a=0$ ($E,E'$ are complexes [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]), so by the universal property of the cokernel $\pi_w$ there are unique $c_1:C_w\to C$, $c_2:C_w\to C'$ with $c_1\pi_w=gp_1$, $c_2\pi_w=g'p_2$. Then $(\mathrm{id}_A,p_1,c_1):E_w\to E$ and $(a,p_2,c_2):E_w\to E'$ are morphisms of short exact sequences ($p_1w=u\circ\mathrm{id}_A$, $p_2w=u'\circ a$). (Stacks omits this; the 'direct sum of two embeddings' device is the standard one, written out by the agent.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof: the verification omitted there ('We omit the verification that this defines a transformation of functors'; 'clearly uniquely determined'), written out by the agent

proof.text: **Step 6 (independence of the choice; definition of $t^{n+1}$).** Let $t^n$ be natural and $E_1,E_2$ two $(n+1)$-effacing sequences with the same left object $A$. Step 5 with $E=E_1$, $E'=E_2$, $a=\mathrm{id}_A$ gives an $(n+1)$-effacing $E_w$ and morphisms $(\mathrm{id}_A,p_1,c_1):E_w\to E_1$, $(\mathrm{id}_A,p_2,c_2):E_w\to E_2$; Step 4 applied to each, with $F^{n+1}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $G^{n+1}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, gives $\tau_{E_1}=\tau_{E_w}=\tau_{E_2}$. Define $t^{n+1}_A:=\tau_E$ for any $(n+1)$-effacing $E$ with left object $A$ (one exists by Step 1); it does not depend on $E$, and by $(\spadesuit)$, $t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C$ for every $(n+1)$-effacing $E$ with left object $A$. (Stacks: 'This is clearly uniquely determined'; the independence of $u$ is written out by the agent.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof: the verification omitted there ('We omit the verification that this defines a transformation of functors'; 'clearly uniquely determined'), written out by the agent

proof.text: **Step 7 ($t^{n+1}$ is a natural transformation).** Let $a:A\to A'$. By Step 1 choose $(n+1)$-effacing $E$ with left object $A$ and $E'$ with left object $A'$. Step 5 gives an $(n+1)$-effacing $E_w$ with left object $A$ and a morphism $(a,p_2,c_2):E_w\to E'$. Step 4 gives $\tau_{E'}\circ F^{n+1}(a)=G^{n+1}(a)\circ\tau_{E_w}$, i.e. by Step 6 $t^{n+1}_{A'}\circ F^{n+1}(a)=G^{n+1}(a)\circ t^{n+1}_A$. So $t^{n+1}:F^{n+1}\to G^{n+1}$ is a natural transformation. (Omitted in Stacks; written out by the agent.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof: the verification omitted there ('We omit the verification that this defines a transformation of functors'; 'clearly uniquely determined'), written out by the agent

proof.text: **Step 8 (every short exact sequence maps to an effacing one with the same left object).** Let $E':0\to A\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ be any short exact sequence. By Step 1 there is a monomorphism $u:A\to I$ with $F^{n+1}(u)=0$. Let $Q$ with $j:B'\to Q$, $k:I\to Q$, $jf'=ku$, be a pushout of $f'$ and $u$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (d). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-pushout-mono] (its $a:=u$, a monomorphism, its $b:=f'$, its $a':=j$), $j$ is a monomorphism, so $m:=jf'=ku:A\to Q$ is a monomorphism (composite of monomorphisms), and $F^{n+1}(m)=F^{n+1}(k)\circ F^{n+1}(u)=0$. With $\pi:Q\to C''$ a cokernel of $m$, $E'':0\to A\xrightarrow{m}Q\xrightarrow{\pi}C''\to0$ is short exact [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (c) and $(n+1)$-effacing. Since $E'$ is exact at $B'$ and $g'$ is an epimorphism [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], $g'$ is a cokernel of $f'$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a); as $\pi jf'=\pi m=0$ there is a unique $c:C'\to C''$ with $cg'=\pi j$. Thus $(\mathrm{id}_A,j,c):E'\to E''$ is a morphism of short exact sequences ($jf'=m\circ\mathrm{id}_A$, $cg'=\pi j$). (Written out by the agent; Stacks only states the compatibility for the chosen sequences.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof: the verification omitted there ('We omit the verification that this defines a transformation of functors'; 'clearly uniquely determined'), written out by the agent

proof.text: **Step 9 (compatibility with $\delta$ for every short exact sequence).** Let $t^n$ be natural, $t^{n+1}$ as in Step 6, and $E':0\to A\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ any short exact sequence; take $E''$ and $(\mathrm{id}_A,j,c):E'\to E''$ from Step 8. Axiom (2) [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] for this morphism gives $\delta^n_{F,E'}=F^{n+1}(\mathrm{id}_A)\circ\delta^n_{F,E'}=\delta^n_{F,E''}\circ F^n(c)$ and likewise $\delta^n_{G,E'}=\delta^n_{G,E''}\circ G^n(c)$. Hence $t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,E'}=t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,E''}\circ F^n(c)=\delta^n_{G,E''}\circ t^n_{C''}\circ F^n(c)$ (Step 6, $E''$ effacing) $=\delta^n_{G,E''}\circ G^n(c)\circ t^n_{C'}$ (naturality of $t^n$) $=\delta^n_{G,E'}\circ t^n_{C'}$. So the square of [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] for morphisms of $\delta$-functors commutes in degree $n$ for every short exact sequence, not only for the chosen ones. (Omitted in Stacks; written out by the agent.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof: the verification omitted there ('We omit the verification that this defines a transformation of functors'; 'clearly uniquely determined'), written out by the agent

proof.text: **Step 10 (existence).** Put $t^0=t$, a natural transformation. If $t^n$ is a natural transformation, Steps 3 and 6 define $t^{n+1}$ (independent of all choices), Step 7 shows it is a natural transformation and Step 9 that $t^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C$ for every short exact sequence $E$. By induction on $n$ this defines natural transformations $t^n:F^n\to G^n$ for all $n\ge0$ with all these squares commuting, i.e. a morphism of $\delta$-functors $(t^n)_{n\ge0}:F\to G$ with $t^0=t$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]. (Stacks: 'We construct $t^n$ by induction on $n$. For $n=0$ we set $t^0=t$.')

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof, first paragraph (induction on n)

proof.text: **Step 11 (uniqueness).** Let $(s^n)_{n\ge0}:F\to G$ be any morphism of $\delta$-functors with $s^0=t$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]. We show $s^n=t^n$ by induction on $n$; $s^0=t=t^0$. If $s^n=t^n$, let $A$ be an object and $E$ an $(n+1)$-effacing sequence with left object $A$ and right object $C$ (Step 1). The compatibility of $s$ with $\delta$ gives $s^{n+1}_A\circ\delta^n_{F,E}=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ s^n_C=\delta^n_{G,E}\circ t^n_C$, so $s^{n+1}_A=\tau_E=t^{n+1}_A$ by the uniqueness in Step 3 (cancel the epimorphism $\delta^n_{F,E}$, Step 2). Hence $s=t$, and $F$ is universal. (Stacks: 'This is clearly uniquely determined by the requirements imposed'.)

source.place: Lemma 010T (lemma-efface-implies-universal), proof, 'This is clearly uniquely determined by the requirements imposed'
